scope: Remaining Browser Sweet Megamono items (M2, M15, M17, M19, M21, M25, M27, M28, M29, M31, M32, M33, M39). Local source changes and local qualification only; no push, npm or Yalc publication, adopter migration, hosted CI or deployment.

items.assessment: Failures write .megamono-create-state.json beside MEGAMONO-RECOVERY.md. `create-megamono <name> --resume` rebuilds the plan from the recorded normalized options, refuses drifted step lists, nothing-completed failures or extra creation flags, reruns the failed step and continues; both recovery files are removed before the atomic rename. A partially applied failed step is rerun, not rolled back.

Not retagged. packages/plugin/README.md records that the generated Chakra theme remains a web runtime adapter with portable tokens living separately, and spec 06 fixes ui -> util only. README now documents the legal homes: one composing ui library plus util logic, a neutral capability:theme-tokens library, type:feature composition, or a reviewed v2 type-direction boundary allowance. A blanket ui -> ui relaxation or theme split is a product decision.

Nx lintProjectGenerator skips the lint target whenever any (even scoped) @nx/eslint/plugin registration exists, so site-then-api workspaces left api, api-e2e, nest-home, site-e2e and --packages libraries without lint. App generation (except Expo) now covers every project it creates with a scoped @nx/eslint/plugin include, replacing @nx/eslint:lint or `eslint <patterns>` targets; create-megamono covers --packages libraries; extension config ignores .output/.wxt. Verified with ESLint 10 that project `files: ['scripts/**']` matches under `eslint .` from the project root and not under the root-cwd executor form. Existing projects are not migrated; README documents convert-to-inferred.

Web UI libraries in a Chakra workspace declare @chakra-ui/react and @emotion/react as peers plus devDependencies (theme already did). Health adds singleton-regular-dependency for libraries declaring react/@chakra-ui/react/@emotion/react in dependencies without a peer; megamono:check prints duplicate installed singletons and non-peer singletons as workspace-dependencies warnings.
megamono:check now prints health's undeclared-workspace-import findings as non-failing workspace-dependencies warnings, outside adoption ratchets and identity baselines (no adopter budget change).

create-megamono bootstrap (workspace-init --bootstrap) appends a repository-owned TypeScript block with no-empty-interface allowSingleExtends and no-empty-object-type allowInterfaces: 'with-single-extends' when the root config uses the Nx TypeScript flat config and neither rule is configured. Verified with ESLint that a later severity-only entry keeps the options. Adopted repositories unchanged.

Not changed to source resolution: nx sync maintains project references and tsc redirects imports of a referenced project's source to its declaration output regardless of export conditions, so the @<scope>/source condition cannot make direct app typecheck read library source. README documents nx typecheck <app> / tsc --build.

App generation declares runtime packages that framework generators added at the root in the generated projects importing them (e2e as devDependencies; app fallback for peers such as rxjs). Root declarations are kept (Nx plugins resolve frameworks from the root; Nx production pruning ignores root devDependencies). New @megamono/plugin:audit-production executor audits one project's `pnpm list --prod --json --depth Infinity --filter` closure against the registry bulk advisory endpoint; generated pnpm apps get an `audit` target. Smoke-tested against registry.npmjs.org.

New prune-build-approvals step after the final install removes only Megamono-pre-seeded `true` approvals for packages absent from pnpm-lock.yaml (e.g. workerd without a Worker app); denials, other entries and later formatting are kept; skipped without a lockfile.

Generated Next launcher resolves PORT, then megamono.json ports.<name> found by walking up from the app, then the planned port, and runs from any directory. Smoke-run with real Node from the app directory with and without PORT. Springbar MCP admission is still not claimed.

Chose bundler-consumable source over a webpack-only site. Fresh TypeScript 5.7+ workspaces set rewriteRelativeImportExtensions in the base config and the library generator writes `./lib/x.ts` re-exports when that option (or allowImportingTsExtensions) is on; tsc still emits `.js`. Reproduced the Turbopack failure with Next 16.4.3 and `.js` specifiers; `.ts` builds with Turbopack and with webpack (+transpilePackages), nodenext/bundler consumers typecheck emitted declarations, Node runs output. Adopted workspaces opt in.

No change. New Next apps (M12) use inferred `next build` with in-place `.next` output and the generated launcher's `next start` in the app directory, so runtime dependencies resolve through the app's node_modules. The dist copy only existed under the legacy @nx/next:build executor; the Nx 17 lane pairs with Next versions predating bundlePagesRouterDependencies.

typescript@7.0.2 (npm latest, checked 2026-11-10) exports only `version` from its main entry (plus ./unstable/* subpaths); createSourceFile, createProgram, resolveModuleName, sys, readConfigFile, parseJsonConfigFileContent, SyntaxKind, forEachChild and the is* guards are undefined. The plugin uses that API in 13 modules (structural/Next/extension boundary analysis, import tooling, ESLint reviewed boundaries), so the typescript peer stays >=5.2 <7. Supporting TS 7 needs a decision (bundle a TS 6 compiler-API dependency or port to the new API). npm publication of next.1 is the user's action.
